pf.license.renewals: A PTIN ends Dec 31 each year: each preparer is reminded 30 days before, and an expired one pauses their bookings. State registrations follow the state form's dates.
pf.license.insurance: A bond or insurance only where the state's form asks; the amount comes from the form.
pf.license.background check: None beyond these checks, unless the state's form asks.

pf.visit.work changes: A form not quoted is priced from the list and added only after a yes. A missing paper: the return waits, and the client uploads it on the secure page.

pf.visit.rejected: A typo: fixed and sent again. Someone already filed with the client's number: the preparer calls, never texts, and explains paper filing and the IRS's identity theft form.

pf.visit.what proves it's done: The code, or DONE, at the sit-down. FILED and ACCEPTED close the return.

notes:
Pilot: from lawyer. Tax prep runs like the lawyer's consult: a first sit-down with a named professional, private papers only on the secure page, a written engagement before the work, and a home visit for someone who can't travel (the lawyer's home signing). Unlike law, a tax office pays Rosfield's $2, has no conflict check and is rated, so those lawyer choices are reversed; the rename lists were rebuilt from the master, so no lawyer words or pairs remain. Coach was the other consult pilot; it was used only to see how a set start time replaces the master's arrival windows.
Cast: Sam Lee owns Lee Tax Services LLC (the master's main company, 700 Main St: tax prep at clients' homes, care homes and hosts' tax days, plus IRS letter help as its second kind of work; trade names Lee Tax Prep and Lee Tax Help) and Lee Tax Office LLC (the second company, 45 Elm St: returns at the office, by video or phone, or as a drop-off). Preparers Kevin Chen and Nina Diaz (the master's Riley and Avery) at the office; Daniel Price, an enrolled agent, and Luis Moore (Jordan and Casey) at Lee Tax Services. Pat stays the office manager; Alex M. stays the customer.
Flow A, the usual side: Alex missed the filing deadline and asks his AI to get him in this week. Rosie books the soonest sit-down with Kevin, Sat Oct 24 at 11:00am. The secure page has the document checklist and uploads, and the office's engagement letter (A4-72). At the desk: the code, a photo ID (two IDs for a new client the preparer doesn't know), the papers list, the return prepared and gone over on screen, Kevin signs as paid preparer with his PTIN, Alex signs the e-file authorization (own split A8-x01), pays $35 at the front desk, then Kevin files and texts FILED; the IRS answers (own split A10-x02: accepted, a typo resent, or already filed with Alex's number, handled by phone only).
Flow B, the less usual side: Alex is home after surgery and books Lee Tax Services to do his late return at 17 Cedar Ln. Daniel comes Thu Oct 22 at a set start, 8:00am (B4-83 '2 A set start time'; the master's arrival-window words are renamed to start times). Same ID check, papers list, return, own signature split B8-x01, the bill texted at DONE, then FILED and the IRS's answer (B10-x01, B10-x02). A tax day at a workplace or senior center is the master's host visit day (B4-66, S1-59).
Prices: the master's numbers are kept as the example offices' own prices, so every sum stays right: simple return $35, itemized return $40, each extra form $20, teen's first return $25, extension filing $55, self-employed return $140, prior-year return quoted from papers ($90), amended return priced at the sit-down ($25 review fee, $110 + a $15 amended state return). At home: return at home $179, $89 trip fee (credited), extension at home $150, back-year returns quoted from papers ($640, over Sam's $500), IRS letter review $149, tax transcript review $199. These are low for real tax offices; see 'Not sure'.
Money paths. A: list|none|counter (main: nothing taken, paid at the front desk when the return is ready to sign, before it's filed), list|none|bill (Saturday mornings Kevin works alone with no front desk, or video: Rosie texts the bill at DONE), photos|none|counter (prior-year return quoted from uploaded papers), visit|none|counter (amended return priced at the sit-down). B: list|none|bill (main), list|none|own (the office's own invoice, or, where it offers it, the fee taken from the refund through its bank partner: a switch in pf.money), photos|none|bill (back-year returns quoted from papers). No holds, saved cards, deposits or full prices: a tax office takes nothing before and has no missed-visit fee by default. The sign-up words (S1-13, S1-14, S1-16, S1-41, S1-42, S1-45 to S1-47) were changed to say so; the master's 'paid in full' extension and fee examples are gone.
Filing waits for the signature and the payment (pf.visit, A10-x01, B10-x01). The fee is never set by the refund, and Rosie never promises a refund, its size or its date (A3-26, A7-12, B3-21, S13-04 more).
Privacy: Social Security and tax ID numbers, income, bank details, refund amounts, letter contents and each preparer's PTIN go only on the secure page. Texts to Alex, Sam and the preparers carry none (A6-15, B6-14, A8-01, B8-01, A8-23, B8-18, S13-05 more). Staff join by replying YES and give their PTIN on the secure page, never by text (S2-05, S2-06, S2-10, S11-48: a change from the master's 'YES with your license number').
Licenses: no company license by default, so S1-60 and S1-63 take the registration branch (registrations 2019-0451 and 2020-1187).
